balloon-application.readScope: Complete actual table/main body read; no infographic/image visual inspection claimed.
balloon-application.fact: The programme uses lighter-than-air helium/hydrogen for lifting balloon payloads, with different envelopes and mission purposes.
balloon-application.limits: Only the helium/property-to-lift case is used. No pupil gas handling, balloon release, pressure-altitude calculations, quantitative buoyancy or full flight inventory.

helium-property.readScope: Actual What-is-helium and selected balloon-use main sections read.
helium-property.fact: Helium is lighter than air and is used as a lifting gas.
helium-property.limits: No inhalation/voice demonstration or blanket safe-gas claim. Unrelated medical/train/current-technology claims and the voice fun-fact are not adopted.

wax-mould.readScope: Actual main directions and cooling/unmoulding instructions read; only melt/pour/cool physical process is used.
wax-mould.fact: The described liquid wax is poured into a mould and cooled until solid before removal.
wax-mould.limits: Read-only attributed case, not instructions for a child to melt/pour wax. No product endorsement, fragrance recipe, burning activity or precise temperature inventory.

air-tyre.publisher: National Museums Scotland, own collection account
air-tyre.readScope: Complete main collection/history body read; photographs not visually inspected for this review.
air-tyre.fact: The museum describes inflated air tubes within tyres and a tested improvement in ride comfort in the particular historical case.
air-tyre.limits: Physical-property application only. No first-invention/date memorisation, universal road-vehicle statement or historical counterfactual adopted.

copper-wire.application: A metal conductor in a low-voltage model circuit/wire
copper-wire.evidence: Actually test suitable copper versus an insulating plastic sample in the same safe battery circuit and record whether the circuit conducts. A simple bulb does not quantify small differences between metals.
copper-wire.explanation: The conducting material lets electrical energy/current be transferred through the designed connection; name electrical conductivity, not an undifferentiated conducts label.

plastic-handle.property: Relatively low thermal conductivity in the selected comparison
plastic-handle.application: A handle that slows transfer of heat from a warmer part
plastic-handle.evidence: Adult-supervised matched-strip warm-water comparison or appropriate safe heat indicator; record actual differences. Do not touch hot cookware or assume every plastic stays safe at every temperature.
plastic-handle.explanation: Under the stated suitable conditions, slowing heat transfer helps keep the held part cooler than a conducting connection. Do not infer the thermal result solely from an electrical test.

water-mould.property: Flows and takes the container shape
water-mould.application: Filling an ice-cube tray before freezing
water-mould.evidence: Actually pour ordinary water into a suitable nonsealed tray and inspect how it occupies the recesses. An adult may supply a separately prepared frozen sample.
water-mould.explanation: Flowing liquid can fill the mould; the later solid retains its shaped form. Allow space for expansion, and distinguish changed state/form from a new substance.

wax-mould.property: Flows into a mould and solidifies on cooling
wax-mould.application: Making a moulded wax shape in the attributed supplier process
wax-mould.evidence: Use the original attributed fact summary of the actually read supplier directions; no pupil hot-wax handling or invented photograph observation.
wax-mould.explanation: The liquid stage allows filling before a solid shape forms. Wax mixtures need not all have one sharp melting point; no exact value is required.

air-tyre.property: Fills an enclosure and is compressible
air-tyre.evidence: Combine the actual museum air-tube application account with an ordinary safe trapped-air bag observation or the existing compression model. A child is not asked to inflate a vehicle tyre or ride a test course.
air-tyre.explanation: Contained air changes volume under a push and pushes back, allowing an inflated flexible tube to yield rather than behave like a rigid wheel. Do not infer that every tyre/pressure/load is equally suitable or calculate gas laws.

helium-balloon.property: Less mass than an equal volume of surrounding air under comparable conditions
helium-balloon.application: Lifting a suitably designed scientific balloon payload
helium-balloon.evidence: Use the actual CSA lighter-than-air gas table and selected BLM property statement as provided factual evidence, not a claimed class launch.
helium-balloon.explanation: The supplied relative-lightness property helps a suitable helium-filled balloon lift; merely being a gas is insufficient, since an otherwise comparable air-filled balloon does not gain that advantage. No quantitative buoyancy equation or new whole density mastery is inferred.

preparation: Prepare the six original attributed application cards, the ordinary actual samples, a fair-test planning frame and an unfilled properties/results/use table. Keep supplied source facts separate from measurements the learner actually makes.

For whole Advanced Material Properties, retain actual distinct tests for the required property repertoire: hardness/scratch resistance, solubility, electrical conductivity and magnetic response, with separate thermal/transparency checks as in the existing guide. Use verified sample identities, a safe low-voltage battery circuit and adult-supervised warm-water setup, with no flame or mains.

For whole Testing Materials, retain an independently planned comparable water-resistance or other meaningful material test, actual measured results and a reason tied to the chosen use. Existing guide placeholders are not observations to be fabricated.
learnerActions: Describe each sample’s state under the stated conditions and its specific relevant physical property, then explain why that property helps the named application. Actually use the solid, liquid AND gas cases, not only availability in the packet.

Run the specified appropriate material/property tests and keep changed, measured and controlled variables distinct; record actual outcomes and cite them for a particular solid-material choice. Separate a test result, a supplied authoritative fact and a modelled consequence.

Explain the two liquid/mould cases: why flow/container shape helps filling and why the later solid form matters. Distinguish the material and its state; do not call all liquids water or all waxes one fixed melting-point substance.

Explain the two gas applications using the particular supplied properties. Air containment/compressibility and helium’s relative lightness support different purposes; neither means every gas rises or all air-filled objects are protective at any pressure.

Give a changed brief: choose between a conducting connection and a cooler handle; choose liquid versus solid material when a recess must be filled; compare air versus helium for a light lifting balloon. Justify from the relevant property/source/test, and name a missing fact if a real design decision cannot yet be made.
successEvidence: Specific property→use explanations across the actual two solid, two liquid and two gas cases, not names or generic material praise.
Evidence cited from actual fair/comparative testing where required and from attributed provided application facts where appropriate.
Distinguishes thermal/electrical conductivity, flow/state/form and gas compressibility/relative lightness without importing quantitative pressure/density/thermal laws.
Complete retained whole material-property/fair-test/state requirements remain separately assessed; component source success is not automatic whole-claim mastery.
nearMisses: Explains only solids and silently omits liquid/gas applications.
Says liquid/gas is useful without explaining which property helps which task.
Declares all metals magnetic, infers heat conduction from electrical results, or treats all gases as lighter than air.
Invents a test table or assumes a source-described professional process was performed by the learner.
protocol.transfer: Original fictional brief: one object needs a conducting connection, another needs an insulating grip, a mould has narrow recesses and a balloon must carry a light instrument. Select suitable supplied materials with reasons and state which further safety/design facts the evidence cannot establish.
